pages.note: Title page: Syllabus for Environmental Sciences/Studies (SCQP11)

Note box (i-iv) then syllabus box; box title "Environmental Sciences/Studies (SCQP11)" repeats the paper title and is not a row; Earth Sciences, Physical and Chemical Sciences, Life Sciences with its sub-headings
last four sub-headings (Global Environmental issues ... Instrumentation)

nodes.label: i
nodes.title: The Question Paper will have 75 questions.

nodes.label: ii
nodes.title: All questions will be based on Subject-Specific Knowledge.
Earth Sciences:
nodes.body: Structure and composition of Environment- Atmosphere, Hydrosphere and Lithosphere, Earth Processes, Mineral and Power Resources in India, Biogeochemical Cycles, Meteorology, Climate Change, Origin and evolution of earth, Mineral and Power Resources in India.

nodes.title: Physical and Chemical Sciences:
nodes.body: Fundamentals, Atmospheric Chemistry, Water Chemistry, Geochemistry, Green Chemistry. Water - physical characteristics, buffering capacity, Essential and trace elements in living systems, Bio-molecules - chemical components of cells, Bio- geochemical cycles – carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus, Hydrological cycle and global water balance, Toxicity of Heavy metals.

nodes.title: Origin of life:
nodes.body: Theories of evolution, genetic drift, speciation, cell organelles, cell division, modes of reproduction, principles of inheritance, epistasis, mutations, chromosomal aberrations,extra- chromosomal inheritance.

nodes.title: Genetic Material:
nodes.body: DNA structure and replication, transcription and translation, chromosome structure, protein structure, mutability and repair of DNA, reverse genetics.

nodes.title: Photosynthesis, Plant growth hormones, Dormancy and seed germination, Respiration
Plant and Animal systematics:
nodes.body: Bryophytes, Tracheophytes, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms. Membrane structure and Ion transport, ATPase - structure and function, Photosynthesis, Photoperiodism, Vernalization, RUBISCO.

nodes.title: Animal systematics, physiology and diseases: Cnidaria, Echinodermata, Chordata, Protostomia; Anatomy and physiology of humans; major classes of bacterial and viral pathogens, Apoptosisand cancer, inherited diseases, animal cell culture.
Ecology and Environment:
nodes.body: Biosphere, Organizational levels of biosphere, Ecosystem: Structure and Types, Food Chain and Energy Flow, Population and Community Ecology, Biodiversity andits Conservation.

nodes.title: Microbiology and Biotechnology:
nodes.body: Principles of Microbiology, Microbiology of Air, Water, Soil, Sewage, Recombinant DNA technology, principles of gene cloning, transposition, applications of biotechnology in medicine, industry, agriculture and environment.

nodes.title: Natural resources and Management:
nodes.body: Natural Resources-Forest, Water, Minerals, Marine, Energy (Renewable and Nonrenewable) - Sources, Threats, Conservation and Management.

nodes.title: Global Environmental issues:
nodes.body: Ozone depletion and Global warming, Acid rain and Smog, Sustainable Development.

nodes.title: Environmental Pollution:
nodes.body: Air, Water, Soil, Noise Pollution- Sources, Causes, Effects, Consequences.

nodes.title: Waste Management:
nodes.body: Solid waste - disposal, Management; Waste to energy conversion.

nodes.title: Instrumentation:
nodes.body: Principles and applications of microscopy, spectrophotometry, centrifugation, radioisotope techniques, electrophoresis and chromatographic separation techniques, Blottingand hybridization techniques.
